text:
cheng: CI red on master: runtime/serve::session_reset_test failing intermittently in the new retry window change. Job: https://ci.internal.redwood/boards/9876/builds/4321 :eyes:

maria: saw this too. repro rate ~1/10 on linux-x86. same test passes locally for me.

sam: can you paste the failing log?

cheng: log snippet: ```
thread 'session_reset_test' panicked at 'expected session active, got closed', runtime/src/session/mod.rs:412
--- last op: retry::backoff (elapsed 123ms)
stack: ...
```

jon: hmm that looks timing-y. test uses a real tokio::time::sleep(15ms) in a loop, plus rng for jitter. possible nondeterministic ordering with the fake scheduler in CI.

maria: CI job env shows GOMAXPROCS=2, whereas my laptop is 8. could be a scheduling difference.

cheng: filing a rerun now: @ci-bot rerun build 4321

ci-bot: rerun queued for build 4321 — started on linux-x86-1 (executor-14).

linda: pinging @sam — you landed the retry-window tweak in PR #2154 yesterday, any quick ideas?

sam: yeah I increased the max jitter a bit to reduce thundering, could be making the window overlap. quick fix: make the test inject a deterministic RNG and use tokio::time::pause() + advance() instead of real sleeps.

jon: +1 for using pause(). Also we should avoid relying on thread scheduling. Should we update the test to use a TestClock?

maria: i can do a small follow-up to replace sleeps with pause()/advance() and inject a seeded rng. low-risk.

cheng: sgtm. can you add a comment in the PR referencing this thread and mark flaky->skip until merged?

maria: will do. quick repro attempt: running 50x with GOMAXPROCS=2 locally now.

ci-bot: rerun complete: build 4321 -> flaky (1/2 failures). failing on executor-14 again. attached logs: https://ci.internal.redwood/boards/9876/builds/4321/logs/err

sam: since rerun reproduced, let's bisect over the last 3 commits touching retry logic. @cheng can you open a bisect job?

cheng: started bisect job: https://ci.internal.redwood/boards/9876/bisect/999 — testing commits range a1b2..c3d4

linda: if bisect points to the jitter change, we should tighten the test expectations rather than revert. But if it's unrelated, we need to look at scheduler invariants.

maria: quick note for the follow-up: modify session_reset_test to use `let mut rng = StdRng::seed_from_u64(42);` + pass rng into RetryPolicy::new_for_test(rng) and use `tokio::time::pause(); tokio::time::advance(Duration::from_millis(...)).await;`

jon: also add a comment about why we prefer deterministic clock/seed in tests to avoid CI flakes.

cheng: thanks. I'll watch the bisect and the PR. tagging this thread for tracking. :memo:
